claim: *Modeling inside the implementation loop.* An engineering problem motivates a model whose analysis informs design and implementation. Measurements test the model’s predictions and expose assumptions that need revision. Modeling and implementation proceed together as new engineering questions arise.
topology: Single feedback loop: problem, model, analysis, prediction/design, implementation, measurement, and a directed revision return to the model.
bw_encoding: White ordinary nodes and groups; labels and boundaries carry roles without decorative tones.
redesign: Panel (a), the linear design/implement/document-with-models chain, was removed on author instruction: the chapter establishes that contrast repeatedly before this point, and the juxtaposition risked implying that modeling conventionally follows implementation, which misdescribes model-driven engineering. The surviving loop was re-laid out to fill the original 920-unit figure width at unchanged font sizes, so rendered label sizes are unchanged rather than magnified. Earlier editorial arrow resolution and grayscale emphasis retained.
alt: A loop. A problem drives a model; analyzing the model yields a prediction and a design; those drive implementation and then measurement; measurement refines the model, and the loop continues while the questions justify the cost.
